name: Self-Directed Dimension
definition: Let $\mathcal H\subseteq\{0,1\}^{X}$ be nonempty on a finite domain. For each $S\subseteq X$, play the following **labelling game** on its initially unlabelled points. In each cycle, Player A labels any subset of the remaining points, possibly empty or all of them. If points remain, Player B chooses one and assigns either binary label. Assigned points are removed. Repeat until all points are labelled, or stop immediately if the accumulated labels are unrealizable by $\mathcal H$. The payoff is $-1$ if unrealizability occurs; otherwise it is the number of moves made by Player B. Player A maximizes and Player B minimizes this payoff. Write $D(\mathcal H,S)$ for its value. The **Self-Directed Dimension** is $\mathrm{SDdim}(\mathcal H)=\max_{S\subseteq X}D(\mathcal H,S)$. For $S=\emptyset$ the value is zero. Player B is permitted to create unrealizability; its labels are not restricted to feasible ones.
graph_summary: Value of the labelling game: A prolongs feasible play, B minimizes its rounds and may force the unrealizable payoff -1.
description: Devulapalli and Hanneke introduced $\mathrm{SDdim}$ as a combinatorial characterization of the optimal self-directed mistake bound.  On the finite binary classes catalogued here it is exactly self-directed queries complexity.

monotonic.proof: By the established equality $\mathrm{SDdim}=\mathrm M_{\mathrm{sd}}$ and subfamily monotonicity of self-directed queries complexity.

c_monotonic.proof: By the established equality $\mathrm{SDdim}=\mathrm M_{\mathrm{sd}}$ and conditioning monotonicity of self-directed queries complexity.
